title: Andy Burnham to tell MPs 'landmark' EU deal could make next decade 'much better'
summary:
The prime minister will tell Parliament on Monday the "landmark" deal struck with the EU means there is a "very real prospect" the next decade can be "much better" than the last one.
The deal, which covers British food exports, emissions trading and a youth experience scheme, is a "choice between a broken status quo or change", Andy Burnham will tell MPs.
The agreements announced on Friday included scrapping most of the checks on British food exports, in return for the UK following some EU regulations, from 2028.
He believes polling suggests the UK public "want closer ties" with the EU and the deal "delivers that".
Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch will use a speech at the Confederation of British Industry (CBI) annual conference on Monday to criticise Burnham's EU deal.

title: What Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia teaches China's Xi about Trump
summary:
Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO has riveted the world - including China, where it has become the top trending post on Weibo, the country's biggest social media platform.
But to many, Huang's return, which is being dubbed one of the greatest U-turns of all time, seems like a vindication for China.
Beijing has dismissed claims that one of the women who had an affair with Jensen Huang had been recruited by China's Ministry of State Security, its version of the CIA, as a spy.
Chinese state media has also framed the spy saga as a smear campaign orchestrated by China hawks in Washington.
Now the White House, and President Donald Trump himself, have said Huang poses no national security threat, although investigations into the spy allegations are still ongoing.

title: Russia threatens ‘hostile’ Estonia with ‘open war’
summary:
Russia has accused Estonia of carrying out numerous “hostile actions” and threatened “open war” against the neighbouring Baltic state.
Russia’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Monday accused Tallinn of a ⁠⁠range of hostile actions, asserting that the NATO and European Union member state is “on ⁠⁠the verge of triggering open war”.
Among a list of additional accusations, the ministry said Estonia had “tacitly allow[ed] its airspace to be used by Ukrainian drones for attacks on northwestern Russia”.
This marked a sharp escalation in tensions between Estonia and Russia, which Tallinn – Kyiv’s ally – sees as part of a broader campaign of hostile activity linked to Moscow’s war in Ukraine.
Russia has long accused Estonia and other NATO states in the Baltic region of allowing Ukrainian drones to use their airspace.

title: How Realistic Are Foreign-Policy Realists?
summary:
Foreign-policy realists are the killjoys of international politics.
They have no choice but to pursue their interests—though realists disagree among themselves about what those are.
“Defensive” realists think states desire security above all.
“Offensive” realists think states are driven to maximize power.
But all realists agree that the laws of power cannot be avoided any more than the law of gravity.

title: US escalates sanctions on Iran, targets ‘shadow banking’ networks
summary:
US Treasury sanctions more than two dozen Iranian entities, citing efforts to disrupt Tehran’s global financial activities, amid ongoing diplomatic effort to end the US-Israel war on Iran.
The Department of the Treasury announced on Monday that it had targeted more than two dozen Iranian exchange houses, front companies, and key personnel with sanctions “in a sweeping effort to disrupt Iran’s global shadow banking networks”.
“Iran’s shadow banking system is the last financial lifeline of a bankrupt regime,” said US Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent.
The US Treasury claimed these entities help Iran “move billions of dollars through the international financial system to provide the regime access to foreign currency despite comprehensive sanctions”.
In addition, “Mina Fashki and Partners Exchange Company (Fashki Exchange) and Mellat Exchange Company” and a number of their owners and employees were designated.

title: Pakistani astronaut to become first foreign visitor to China’s space station
summary:
Three astronauts will launch aboard China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft.Credit: Xinhua/ShutterstockFor the first time, China will send a foreign astronaut to its Tiangong space station.
Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a Pakistani military pilot, is expected to travel to Tiangong on 25 November aboard China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft, alongside two Chinese astronauts, known as ‘taikonauts’.
Sending an astronaut to space is “a huge step” for Pakistan’s space aspirations, says Wajiha Iqbal, a lunar scientist at the University of Münster in Germany.
The mission is also a milestone for China’s space programme.

summary:

Zelensky added that Ukraine's attack hit a second Russian vessel, a cargo ship which he claimed was being used to transport weapons.

summary:

title: How the US, China and Russia are competing for Africa’s mineral wealth
summary:
The US, China and Russia are vying for Africa’s mineral wealth, raising questions about who stands to benefitShare How the US, China and Russia are competing for Africa’s mineral wealth on social mediaFrom cobalt mines in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) to lithium deposits in Mali and uranium reserves in Niger, Africa’s mineral wealth is becoming an increasingly important arena of competition between the United States, China and Russia.
China dominates several critical mineral supply chains, while Russia has expanded its influence through security partnerships, particularly in the Sahel.
But as foreign powers compete for access, what do African countries stand to gain?
China has spent years investing in African mining, processing and infrastructure.
As Washington, Beijing and Moscow compete for Africa’s mineral wealth, the real test for African countries may be not which global power wins the race, but how much of the wealth they can retain.

title: Russia makes a new ballistic missile every 5 hours and is picking up the pace, Ukraine warns
summary:
Russia produces one ballistic missile every five hours and is working to accelerate this pace, Ukrainian Defense Minister Yevhenii Khmara said on Monday.
Over the weekend, Russia launched a massive bombardment against Ukraine using roughly 110 missiles, including over two dozen ballistic missiles, and more than 400 drones.
"Every five hours," the defense minister said, "the enemy produces one ballistic missile and continues to accelerate this pace.
Earlier this month, Ukraine's military intelligence agency released a new assessment detailing Russian missile stockpiles and production capacity.
It said that as of October, Moscow's reserves included up to 700 ballistic missiles and thousands of cruise missiles.
